sentences.text:
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Petitioners seek quashing of FIR No. 86/2020 of PS G.T.B Enclave for offence under Section 498-A/406/34 IPC on the ground that complainant de facto (respondent no.2) has compromised the disputes with the petitioners.
3. Learned APP appearing with IO/SI Arvind accepts notice and seeks and is allowed four weeks to file status report.
4. The IO submits that he was informed by the petitioners and respondent no.2 that they are unable to appear today.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 05/01/2026 at 20:32:46 5.
I have examined the subject FIR.
It does not appear to be a regular case of Section 498A/406 IPC.
It is alleged in the FIR that the petitioners tried to kill the respondent no.2 by dousing her with oil and trying to burn her but she saved herself and ran away.

Further, the allegation in the FIR is also for offence under Section 4 of Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act as the petitioner no.1 pronounced triple talaq on respondent no.2, so she must be heard in view of Section 7(b) of the Act.
